Welcome to Osmani Primary School.
At Osmani, we offer our pupils and staff the opportunity to be creative, innovative and adventurous in their approach to learning and teaching. We use approaches and strategies that value effort, perseverance, co-operation, collaboration, problem-solving and leadership skills within an inclusive, happy and stimulating learning environment. Read more.
See our Instagram page for updates!
We are a Rights Respecting School. Click here for more information.

Cookies and Privacy
Cookies
Individual services on our website may ask you to set cookies to remember you on this device. You don't need to accept these cookies for the services to work and you can delete them at any time.
Tracking
We track the pages you visit on this site using Google Analytics. This tells us what's popular so we can do more of what you like.
Tracking is optional and even if you have it turned on we aren't collecting any personal data about you.
Privacy
Any personal data that you send us will generally be kept for five years before the records are removed. Each service on this site will inform you how your data will be stored and transferred before you submit it.
You can ask to see what details we hold about you and request that they be removed at any time by contacting us in writing.

Year 5 children had a fantastic time taking part in the Spitalfields' BIG SING performance, joining voices with pupils from other schools across Tower Hamlets. The event was a joyful celebration of music and teamwork, giving the children a chance to perform in a large choir and experience the excitement of singing on a big stage. Through rehearsals and the final performance, they built confidence, made new friends, and created wonderful memories as part of this inspiring musical collaboration.
This experience reflects Article 31 of the UN Convention on the Rights of the Child, which states that every child has the right to relax, play and take part in a wide range of cultural and artistic activities.
You can view more on the Spitalfield Music website.

Rights Respecting Ambassadors
We are a Gold Rights Respecting School.
At Osmani, we are extremely proud to have achieved the Gold accreditation as part of the Rights Respecting Schools Award. A Rights Respecting ethos is at the heart of everything we do at Osmani, helping us to ‘fulfil our potential and reach for the stars’. The award recognises achievement in putting the UN Convention on the Right of the Child (UNCRC) at the heart of a school’s practice to improve well-being and help all children ‘reach for the stars’.
You can read about what our assessor thought of our RRSA work in Summer 2025:
Level 1/Silver Report
Level 2/Gold Accreditation Report
Level 2/Gold Reaccreditation Report
Level 2/Gold Reaccreditation Report
Where do the Rights come from?
On the 20th November 1989, world leaders came together and made a comprehensive set of promises to every child on earth, to ensure that they grow up in the spirit of peace, dignity, tolerance, freedom, equality and solidarity. The United Nations Convention on the Rights of the Child is an international statement of all of those promises. UNICEF protects and promotes those rights.
These rights try to make sure that every child is healthy, receives an education, is treated fairly and is always listened to. They also make sure that all children are safe and protected from violence, abuse and exploitation.
Have a closer look at The UNICEF Rights in Child Friendly Language – Convention Rights
Who are the Rights Respecting Ambassadors?
The Osmani School Rights Respecting Ambassadors are a representative group of pupils elected by their peers to represent their views and raise issues concerning them. The group is made up of two representatives (a boy and a girl) from each class from year 2 to year 6 including pupils with SEND. Rights Respecting Ambassadors bring the views expressed in class to council meetings. During these sessions, ambassadors discuss areas that are going well within the school, areas for improvement and make requests on behalf of their peers. These views are then fed back to the school’s senior leadership team, teachers and pupils.

The Rights Respecting Ambassadors have chosen Cancer Research UK as the charity of the year.
Rights Respecting Meetings:
Meetings are held weekly on Fridays from 2:30pm to 3:00pm. Topics covered last year have included health and safety, trips and visits, lunchtime issues and the curriculum.

Admissions
The policy and arrangements for admission to the school are set out in the Local Authority's school admissions booklet 'Starting School in Tower Hamlets', which can be accessed at www.towerhamlets.gov.uk/schooladmissions. A paper copy can be obtained from the Local Authority's Pupil Admissions Team on tel: 020 7364 5006.
For information about Nursery to Reception please click here.
For information about In-Year Transfers please click here.
Admission to the Nursery
The school admits children using the admission criteria and guidelines agreed by London Borough of Tower Hamlets.
At Osmani, we offer part-time Nursery places. However, we will offer a full-time place if you meet the national criteria. Children born in an admission year e.g children born between 1st September and 31st August are staggered in, between September to November, where the oldest children in the cohort for that year start first.
Most nursery-aged children start school in our Nursery after their third birthday. Children starting Nursery will usually be visited at home by members of the Early Years team before admission and will be invited for Parent-Toddler sessions in the summer term.
Pupils admitted to the school will need to complete a starter pack, adhere to a code of conduct, and sign a home-school agreement. Parents are also expected to adhere to all school policies.
Applying for 3-year-old Nursery places at Osmani:
If your child turns three between the 1st of September and the 31st of March and you would like a nursery place for January or April, you must apply online on Synergy Admissions.
Please note that a place in the Nursery does not guarantee a place in the Reception class. For move up to Reception you will need to reapply via the eAdmission website.

Unlocking Potential (UP Foundation)
UP Foundation is a school-based charity offering therapeutic support to both children and their families.
Being a child can sometimes be a confusing and stressful time. The Unlocking Potential Foundation offers children who find themselves in challenging situations. A weekly space is provided so they can meet with a grown-up outside of their family to help them understand and manage their feelings and emotions. This can also be a creative time where they can learn themselves through play and the arts. Therapy is provided by both qualified and trainee therapists.
The UP team works closely with parents and school staff to ensure they offer the most appropriate help and achieve the best possible outcomes for the child. They do this through individual therapy sessions, group sessions, lunchtime, and after-school clubs, as well as fun days and school trips.
The Therapy Team Manager in Osmani Primary School is Katie Willmore, please talk to your child’s teacher or the school reception if you would like to find out more about our service or arrange to meet Eunice.
You can also visit www.up.org.uk to find out more about The Schools Programme and Unlocking Potential.

About Tower Hamlets EBP and Partner Schemes
THEBP supports the education, training and development of young people by building partnerships between 66 primary schools in the Borough and businesses in the City and Canary Wharf. We recruit volunteers to support pupils with their key skills, as well as develop confidence, and act as a positive role models.
Reading Partners is our most popular scheme, where business volunteers support pupils with reading and comprehension for 30 minutes, on a weekly or fortnightly basis. Many schools also have Number, Chess Partners, which follow a similar model.

Rights Respecting Ambassadors
We are a Gold Rights Respecting School.
At Osmani, we are extremely proud to have achieved the Gold accreditation as part of the Rights Respecting Schools Award. A Rights Respecting ethos is at the heart of everything we do at Osmani, helping us to ‘fulfil our potential and reach for the stars’. The award recognises achievement in putting the UN Convention on the Right of the Child (UNCRC) at the heart of a school’s practice to improve well-being and help all children ‘reach for the stars’.
You can read about what our assessor thought of our RRSA work in Summer 2025:
Level 1/Silver Report
Level 2/Gold Accreditation Report
Level 2/Gold Reaccreditation Report
Level 2/Gold Reaccreditation Report
Where do the Rights come from?
On the 20th November 1989, world leaders came together and made a comprehensive set of promises to every child on earth, to ensure that they grow up in the spirit of peace, dignity, tolerance, freedom, equality and solidarity. The United Nations Convention on the Rights of the Child is an international statement of all of those promises. UNICEF protects and promotes those rights.
These rights try to make sure that every child is healthy, receives an education, is treated fairly and is always listened to. They also make sure that all children are safe and protected from violence, abuse and exploitation.
Have a closer look at The UNICEF Rights in Child Friendly Language – Convention Rights
Who are the Rights Respecting Ambassadors?
The Osmani School Rights Respecting Ambassadors are a representative group of pupils elected by their peers to represent their views and raise issues concerning them. The group is made up of two representatives (a boy and a girl) from each class from year 2 to year 6 including pupils with SEND. Rights Respecting Ambassadors bring the views expressed in class to council meetings. During these sessions, ambassadors discuss areas that are going well within the school, areas for improvement and make requests on behalf of their peers. These views are then fed back to the school’s senior leadership team, teachers and pupils.
